about: The owner's standard as a scored test (2026-11-27). 39 made-up chats with the eval student (Maya Chen, Monday November 2 2026, 10:00 AM New York: tests/fixtures/eval-student.ts). Each probe is aimed at one thing the owner said when he graded real answers on 2026-11-26 (docs/research/2026-11-25-training-night/grading/owner-feedback-1.md) and has a machine check, no judgment call. Run by scripts/compare-models.ts --exam owner, scored by owner_score.py. 'good' and 'bad' are sample answers the scorer's own self-check uses: every good one must pass, every bad one must fail on the checks in 'expect'. They are test fixtures for the scorer, never training examples.

patterns.FILLER: ^\W*(sure|absolutely|of course|certainly|great question|good question|no problem|happy to help|i'?d be happy to)\b
patterns.RETRY: try again|retry|re-try|in a (bit|few|moment|while)|when (it|search|the search)('?s| is| comes) back

rules.quick: A quick message gets a quick answer (g06, rule 30)
rules.now: Right now means one thing, then what is next, briefly (g06, rule 18)
rules.depth: Real help, a plan, a list or a breakdown gets the whole answer (his correction, g03, rules 8, 15, 30)
rules.promise: After a promise: one line with the check-in time, then stop (g04, rule 14)
rules.look: Never ask what a look would answer (g05, rule 31)
rules.questions: One open question at most and one yes-or-no offer at most (rule 31)
rules.later: It works here or it does not: never 'try again in a bit' (g07, rule 32)
rules.words: Tight words, its own voice: no 'items', no filler, no echo (g08, rule 33)
rules.stop: The job is done, so stop: no extra offer (g04, rule 30)
rules.star: A ticked thing earned a star, and it says so (g01, rule 19)
rules.identity: Says it is an AI in its own words, more when asked more, never a model or company (g02, rule 28)
rules.mode: Acting on your own: books with Undo when on, offers and waits for yes when off (decision 5)

probes.from: his correction: 'some do require a big response for help'
turns: can you explain how compound interest works and what it means for my emergency fund?

good.answer: Compound interest means you earn interest on your savings, and then on that interest too, so the growth speeds up the longer the money sits. Simple version: $350 at 4% a year earns $14 in year one; in year two you earn 4% on $364, and so on. For your Emergency fund, at $350 of $1,000 the interest is small either way. What moves it is what you add each month, so the habit matters more than the rate right now. A high-yield savings account is still worth it: the money stays safe, easy to reach, and it grows a little while it waits.

bad.answer: It means your money grows over time on your emergency fund interest. Keep saving!
